description: A small pile of pale, curled wood shavings at the bottom of the cavity, fresh and smelling of sap.
A scattering of dry, aged wood shavings, mixed with dust and a few tiny, dried-out beetle husks.
A handful of fine, sawdust-like shavings, so light they almost float when you breathe on them.
A single, stiff, black-and-white barred feather, from the woodpecker that carved this hole.
A small, downy red feather, from a woodpecker's crown, tucked into a splinter.
A small, brown, speckled feather, from a bird that briefly nested here.
A soft, pale blue feather, from an egg-layer who used this hole as a nursery.
A single, soft, grey-and-white downy feather, caught in a rough edge of the cavity.
A fragment of pale blue eggshell, dry and brittle, left over from a bird's nest.
A cluster of broken, speckled eggshells, pushed to one side by a previous tenant.
A single, perfect, unhatched egg, small and cold, long abandoned.
A small, dark beetle, its shell dull with dust, sitting motionless in the shadows.
A long, thin, brown beetle, its antennae waving as it crawls along the inner wall.
A cluster of tiny, black beetles, huddled together in a corner of the cavity.
A small, pale, wingless insect, scuttling away from the light.
A silverfish, its body covered in fine, shimmering scales, slipping into a crack.
A small, dried-out insect husk, so light it crumbles at a touch.
A small, pale moth, resting on the inner wall, its wings folded flat.
A dusty, grey moth, its wings tattered, hiding in the darkest corner.
A small, dark spider, sitting in a silk-lined nook, watching.
A small, dusty spiderweb, filling the entrance, strung with tiny, dried husks.
A small, round, white egg sac, tucked into a crevice, covered in fine silk.
A long, reddish-brown centipede, curled around a splinter, its legs rippling.
A small, dark millipede, coiled into a tight spiral in the damp wood dust.
A small, grey woodlouse, rolled into a ball in the darkest corner.
A single black ant, exploring the cavity, its antennae tapping the walls.
A cluster of small, reddish ants, carrying tiny crumbs of wood into a crack.
A small patch of soft, green moss, growing in the damp corner of the cavity.
A thick, dark green cushion of moss, filling the base of the hollow.
A pale, silver-green lichen, crusting the inner wall in a ruffled pattern.
A small, pale, shelf-like fungus, growing out of the damp wood.
A cluster of tiny, pale mushrooms, growing in the darkness of the hollow.
A single, thin, translucent mushroom, growing sideways from the inner wall.
A small, brown, capped mushroom, growing from a crack in the damp wood.
A single, pale, delicate mushroom, growing in the leaf litter at the base of the cavity.
A tiny, delicate bone, bleached white, half-buried in the wood dust.
A small, fragile bird bone, hollow and light, tucked into a crevice.
A single, small vertebra, like a tiny wheel, resting on the floor of the cavity.
A larger bone, weathered and grey, wedged into the back of the hollow. Something lived here once.
A thick, curved rib bone, half-buried in the debris, from an old kill.
A small tuft of soft, grey fur, caught on a splinter, from a squirrel that nested here.
A patch of coarse, reddish-brown fur, from a raccoon that used this hollow as a den.
A single, dark, bristly hair, from something larger. You don't want to think about what.
A large, glossy black feather, from a crow, tucked into a corner.
A long, grey-and-white striped feather, from an owl that roosted here.
A single, small, hard nut, wedged into a crack in the inner wall.
A small pile of acorns, carefully hoarded in a corner by a squirrel.
A cracked, empty hazelnut shell, resting in the wood dust.
A single, shiny chestnut, perfectly preserved, tucked into the hollow.
A perfect acorn, still in its cap, resting alone on the floor.
A scattering of empty acorn caps, left over from a squirrel's feast.
A small, closed pinecone, wedged into a splinter, its scales tight.
A large, open pinecone, stripped of its seeds, resting on the floor.
A chewed pinecone core, stripped bare by a squirrel, dry and brittle.
A thin, dry twig, snapped off and shoved into a corner.
A small bundle of twigs, carefully arranged as if for a nest that was never finished.
A short, straight stick, about the length of a finger, wedged into the back of the cavity.
A single, dry, curled leaf, blown in long ago, now brittle and crumbling.
A small pile of dry leaves, packed tightly together in a corner.
A fresh, green leaf, still soft, recently blown in.
A tiny, hard, black seed, resting in a crevice.
A single, winged maple seed, caught in the wood dust.
A small, dry, brown seed pod, resting on the floor.
A single, dried, golden drop of sap, hardened into a smooth bead.
A long, amber-colored trail of dried sap, running down the inner wall.
A hard, translucent, golden lump of pine resin, smooth and cool to the touch.
A sticky, fresh blob of resin, clinging to the wood and smelling sharply of pine.
A small, amber-colored chip of dried sap, brittle and clear.
A tiny, spiral snail shell, empty and dry, resting in the damp corner.
A small cluster of empty snail shells, huddled together in the dark.
A small, white, freshwater shell, smooth and cool, tucked into a crevice.
A small, tarnished copper coin, resting in the wood dust, forgotten long ago.
A silver coin, wedged into a splinter, its face worn smooth.
A tiny, ancient gold coin, half-buried in the debris.
A small, blue glass marble, resting alone in the corner, catching the dim light.
A white, chipped marble, wedged into a crack in the inner wall.
A single, round, wooden button, resting in the wood dust.
A tiny, ornate brass button, green with age, tucked into a crevice.
A tiny, blue glass bead, half-buried in the debris.
A short, faded scrap of red ribbon, caught on a splinter.
A small, dusty scrap of fabric, faded and frayed, wedged into a corner.
A short piece of twine, tied into a small, tight knot.
A small, rusty nail, driven into the inner wall long ago.
A single, dried oak gall, rolling loose on the floor.
A single, cylindrical owl pellet, dry and grey, packed with fur and tiny bones.
A small pile of owl pellets, older ones crumbling into dust at the edges.
A small pile of dark, dry, crumbly droppings beneath a narrow crevice.
A scattering of tiny, dark, oblong droppings, fresh and glossy.
A single, cylindrical dropping, packed with fur and small bones.
An old, abandoned nest, made of twigs and dried grass, crumbling at the edges.
A small, soft nest, lined with feathers and fur, long since abandoned.
A weathered, hollow ball of leaves and twigs, the remains of a squirrel's drey.
A small, papery egg case, empty and dry, wedged into a splinter.
A long, dry, translucent snakeskin, caught on a splinter, trailing into the darkness.
A small, perfect, shed skin, coiled in a corner like a tiny ghost.
A small, dark snake, coiled in the deepest part of the hollow, watching you.
A small, brown toad, sitting in the damp corner, blinking slowly.
A tiny, green tree frog, clinging to the inner wall, its throat pulsing.
A small, brown lizard, basking in a patch of light that reaches into the cavity.
A grey squirrel, peeking out from the hollow, its eyes bright and curious.
A messy, warm ball of leaves and twigs, filling one side of the hollow.
A small, golden piece of honeycomb, wedged into a corner, still smelling of honey.
A small, papery wasp nest, tucked into the back of the hollow, long abandoned.
A small, folded note, tucked into a crack in the inner wall. It reads: 'I hid something here. I forgot what.'
A scrap of paper, stained and crumpled: 'If you found this hole, you found my hiding spot. I hope you left something behind.'
A tiny note, written in a shaky hand: 'I was hiding from something. It is gone now. So am I.'
A note, written on a scrap of birch bark: 'Treasure map. X marks the... actually, I forget where I put the treasure.'
A small, rolled-up note, tied with a thread: 'I left this note for whoever finds this hollow. Hello. I hope you are well.'
A crumpled note, written in a rush: 'DO NOT LOOK IN THE BACK. Okay, you looked. How was it?'
A note, written in very neat, tiny handwriting: 'I lived here for three days during a storm. It was cozy. 10/10.'
A tiny scrap of paper: 'The previous tenant left no forwarding address. Rude.'
A note, tucked into the deepest corner: 'I hid my favorite rock here. It is gone now. I am sad.'
A note, written in confident, looping script: 'Whoever finds this hole, consider it yours now. I have moved on to bigger holes.'
A note, written in berry juice, faded: 'I stored my winter nuts here. Please do not eat them. (They are probably gone by now.)'
A small, folded note, written by a child: 'This is my secret hiding spot. You are not allowed to know about it. — Signed, someone.'
A note, written on leather: 'I came back to check on my stash. It is empty. I blame the squirrels.'
A note, written in very shaky handwriting: 'If you're reading this, I am probably still in the tree. Do not tell anyone.'
A tiny note, tucked into a splinter: 'The owls know. They always know.'
A sad little note: 'I left this here when I was young. I came back to find it. It is still here. So am I.'
A sweet note, written in careful cursive: 'I hid a kiss here for you. It is gone now, but the thought remains.'
A note, written in very official-looking script: 'NOTICE: This hollow is the private property of the squirrel who lives here. Please vacate immediately.'
A note, written in a tiny, precise hand: 'I have counted every acorn in this hollow. There are 37. Please do not disturb them.'
A note, folded into a tiny paper ball: 'I folded this note to make it small. It is still a note. I am still here.'
A note, written in very faint pencil: 'If you can read this, please add your name to the list. — [a single, faded name is written below, illegible]'
A note, written in very careful, elegant script: 'I came here to hide from the world. The world found me. So I hid here instead.'
A small, dark, heavy coin, stamped with a symbol you don't recognize.
A coin made of an unfamiliar metal, cool and oddly heavy, resting at the bottom of the hollow.
A small, tarnished silver ring, half-buried in the wood dust. It has no stone.
A simple copper band, green with age, wedged into a splinter.
A small, rusty iron key, resting in a corner. It opens something, somewhere.
A tiny, ornate brass key, warm to the touch, tucked into a crevice.
A small, dented silver thimble, resting on its side in the debris.
A simple brass thimble, worn smooth, half-buried in the wood dust.
A small, carved wooden whistle, shaped like a bird, resting in the corner.
A tiny brass bell, tarnished and silent, tucked into the hollow.
A small, silver bell, no bigger than a thumbnail, resting in the wood dust.
A single, smooth, wooden bead, dark with age, resting in a corner.
A small, blue glass bead, catching the dim light that reaches into the hollow.
A cluster of tiny, seed-like beads, threaded loosely on a frayed string.
A single, small, brown egg, intact but cold, resting in a soft bed of moss.
A fragment of a larger, speckled eggshell, edges jagged.
A cluster of tiny, pale eggs, laid in a jelly-like mass in the damp corner.
A small cluster of pale green mushrooms, glowing faintly in the darkness.
A single, luminous mushroom, growing from the damp wall, casting a soft light.
A single feather that shimmers faintly with its own soft light, tucked into a crevice.
A small, perfectly smooth stone, cool and dark, resting in the wood dust.
A single, pale stone that glows faintly in the darkness, giving off a soft warmth.
A small, clear crystal, sharp-edged and cool, tucked into a splinter.
A cluster of tiny, pale crystals, growing in the damp corner, catching the dim light.
A final note, tucked into the deepest part of the hollow: 'If you have read all the notes in this hollow, you are the first. Congratulations. Please leave one of your own.'
A small, smooth stone, glowing with a faint, sickly green light. It has been buried a long time. Birds are not fond of these ones.
A small, smooth stone, glowing with a warm, golden light, tucked into a corner of the hollow. Birds are fond of them and often tuck them away in places like this.
A small, smooth stone, its glow almost gone. Only the faintest trace of pink light remains, like a candle running out of wax.
A small glowstone with a thin crack running through it. Its light flickers as if in pain, pulsing unevenly.
Two glowstones nestled together, one blue and one amber, their lights mingling into a soft, quiet lavender.
A single, silver-white moonpetal, dried and folded shut. It will not open again, but it still glows faintly in the dark.
A single moonpetal, pressed flat and preserved, tucked between two thin strips of bark. Someone wanted to keep it.
A small, dark fragment of bark, covered in dust, showing no stars at all until you wipe it clean. Then they appear, one by one.
A small fragment of bark, its stars faded and grey, like a sky at dawn. The stars move slower than they should.
A small, pale leaf, tucked into the deepest part of the hollow. It whispers back whatever you say, but only after a long pause, as if thinking.
A pale leaf, its whisper cracked and thin. It repeats your words, but they come out broken.
A small, papery pod, hanging from a splinter, unlit and cool. Whatever once lit it is gone.
A tiny, glowing pod, smaller than the others, wedged into a crack. Its light pulses slowly, like breathing.
A hollow knot in the wood, silent when the wind passes. The note it once hummed has been forgotten.
A deep, hollow knot that hums a single, low note when the wind reaches into it. The note is older than the tree.
A single, frozen dewdrop that never melts, resting on the inner wall of the hollow. It hums a tiny, high note when touched.
A single, frozen dewdrop, dark and cloudy inside. Something is trapped within, but it does not move.
A small strip of bark with faint, glowing runes carved into it. The runes spell a single word: 'wait.'
A strip of bark, its runes dark and cold. They stopped glowing long ago, but they are still sharp to the touch.
A single, pale egg, cold to the touch, humming a slow, sad tune. It has been alone for a long time.
A small, warm egg, humming a cheerful, wandering melody. It feels happy to be found.
A small tangle of dream-silk, woven into a loose nest in the corner. Half-formed images drift across it — a forest, a face, a falling star.
A single strand of dream-silk, snagged on a splinter, shimmering with faint, shifting colors. It remembers being dreamt.
A single ember-leaf, no longer glowing. It is cold and dark, and crumbles into ash at the touch. Something once burned here.
A single ember-leaf, glowing brightly in the darkness of the hollow, warm but not burning. It lights the entire cavity.
A moon-acorn with a thin crack in its shell. Its silver light leaks out in slow, gentle pulses, like a heartbeat.
Two moon-acorns nestled together, their silver lights mingling into a soft, quiet glow. They are warm to the touch.
A small, clear crystal with a hairline crack running through it. It hums two notes at once, slightly out of tune, like a duet that never quite agreed.
A tiny, arched door, no bigger than your thumb, set into the inner wall of the hollow. It is closed, and warm to the touch. Light leaks faintly from beneath it.
A tiny, wrapped bundle, no bigger than a thumbnail, tied with a strand of spider silk. It hums faintly and smells of honey.
